basic_details.job_title: Prakasam District Court Special Judicial Magistrate Recruitment 2026 – Apply Offline
basic_details.short_information: The District Judiciary, Prakasam District, through the Principal District and Sessions Judge, Ongole, has invited applications for the vacant posts of Special Judicial Magistrate of II-Class at 11 courts in Chirala, Giddalur, Kandukur, Markapur, Ongole, Addanki, Darsi, Kanigiri and Podili. Retired judicial, ministerial and gazetted officers and advocates no longer on the Bar Council rolls may apply in the enclosed format. Applications must be received on or before 19 December 2026 up to 5:00 PM; postal or courier delays will not be considered.

age_limit.details: Non-practising advocates with a practice at the Bar of not less than five years must be above 45 years and below 65 years of age. Retired persons must have at least one and half years (1½ years) to complete 65 years of age. Age is counted as on the date of Notification (21 November 2026). The notice does not mention any age relaxation.

Public Service Commission, and who has exercised Magisterial powers during his tenure of service for not less than three years. | A suitable retired Judicial Officer shall be given preference. | An applicant under clause (iv) (advocate) shall enclose a certificate from the competent authority that he had a practice at the Bar for not less than five years, together with a Certificate of Suspension of Practice issued by the State Bar Association. An applicant who is a Retired Officer of the Revenue Department shall enclose a certificate from the competent authority that he exercised Magisterial powers for not less than three years during his tenure of service in the Gazetted cadre. | Non-practising advocates with a practice at the Bar of not less than five years must be above 45 years and below 65 years of age. Retired persons must have at least one and half years (1½ years) to complete 65 years of age. Age is counted as on the date of Notification (21 November 2026). The notice does not mention any age relaxation. | The following persons shall not be eligible: | A practising advocate. A member of any State or Legal Authority. A member of the State Legislature or of the Parliament. A person who, having held an office under the State or the Union Government or any local authority, has been dismissed, removed or compulsorily retired from service, or subjected to any other major penalty for misconduct. A person convicted and sentenced by a court for an offence involving moral delinquency, or charged with any offence constituting moral turpitude with proceedings pending. A person of unsound mind, or who is deaf, mute or blind, or suffering from leprosy or any other contagious disease. A person in a bigamous marriage. A woman whose marriage is void because the husband had a wife at the time of the marriage, or who has married a person who had a wife living at the time of the marriage. A person adjudicated as an insolvent or an undischarged insolvent. A contractor, businessman or one interested in a subsisting contract or any work being done for the Central or State Government or a local authority within whose limits the Special Judicial Magistrate of II-Class has to discharge his duties. | Honorarium: Rs.45,000/- per month and Rs.5,000/- per month towards conveyance charges, as per G.O.Rt.No.229, Law (L and LA & J Home-Courts.A) Department, dated 04.03.2026, subject to enhancement from time to time by the Government. Unit of appointment: since the Judicial Districts are not bifurcated for the Judiciary in Andhra Pradesh, the unit of appointment shall be the respective Judicial District to which the candidate belongs, except as otherwise provided. Court hours: court work for 5 days a week, Monday to Friday, on working days from 7.30 am to 10.30 am. Leave: Casual Leave not exceeding 15 days in a calendar year; no other kind of leave. Tenure: the courts at Sl.No.8 to 11 (Addanki, Darsi, Kanigiri, Podili) are sanctioned under the 13th Finance Commission, and their term will be till 31-03-2027. Powers conferred on a Special Judicial Magistrate of II Class automatically stand withdrawn on attaining the age of 65 years. | A complaint of misconduct received by the High Court is placed before the Committee dealing with the subject; if the Committee finds misconduct or dereliction of duty, a show cause notice is issued requiring the officer to explain. After considering the explanation, the Committee may recommend termination of services, which is forwarded to the Government; the order so passed is final. A Special Judicial Magistrate of II Class may be removed without being called upon to show cause if he or she fails to attend three consecutive sittings of the court without the written permission of the concerned Chief Judicial Magistrate. | Candidates should check the official notification for the full eligibility conditions that apply to each post.

important_instructions: The notice states that candidates intending to apply for more posts must submit a single application, clearly mentioning the order of preference for the place of posting, instead of multiple applications for each vacant post. The notice also contains a line stating that an applicant applying for more than one post should submit a separate application for each post with all enclosures, and that common applications will be summarily rejected. Candidates should verify this detail from the latest official notice. Applications with insufficient information and without proof of certificates will be rejected, and no further correspondence will be made. content_sections.heading: About Prakasam District Court Recruitment 2026
content_sections.text: The notification has been issued by the Principal District and Sessions Judge, Ongole, for the District Judiciary of Prakasam District in Andhra Pradesh. It refers to the High Court's Letter in ROC.No.515/SO/2021, dated 09.09.2024, along with Notification No.19/SO/2024 (The Andhra Pradesh Special Judicial Magistrate of II-Class Rules, 2024). Seven of the courts are listed as Regular Courts, and four courts (Sl.No.8 to 11) are sanctioned under the 13th Finance Commission vide G.O.Ms.No.35, Law (LA &J.Home Courts-C) Department, dated 31-03-2011; their tenure, with supporting staff, has been extended till 31-03-2027 as per G.O.Ms.No.299, Law (Home-Courts.A) Department, dated 17.03.2026.

content_sections.heading: Where and How to Send
content_sections.text: Applications are invited in the format enclosed with the notification, for the posts in the Unit of District Judge, Prakasam. The notification is issued by the Principal District and Sessions Judge, Ongole; it does not print a separate postal address with a PIN code for sending applications. The last date for receiving applications is 19 December 2026, and applications received after 5:00 PM on 19 December 2026 will not be considered under any circumstances. Postal and courier delays will not be considered. The application format (page 5 of the notification) is headed "Application for the post of Special Judicial Magistrate of Second Class at 1)... 2)... 3)... Etc.", where the places are written in order of preference. It asks for: Name (full name in block letters) Father's Name Date of Birth Permanent Address Address for communication with mobile number Educational Qualifications Professional Experience, if any Whether worked previously as Spl. Judicial Magistrate of Second Class, and if so, the period and place(s) Whether the applicant belongs to OC/SC/ST/BC Service in Government, if any, and Date of Retirement Particulars of practice as an advocate (period to be specified) Whether the applicant has exercised Magisterial Powers for not less than three years, with the period (proof to be enclosed) Any other information the applicant wishes to furnish The form ends with Station, Date and the signature of the applicant. Candidates applying for more than one post must follow the instruction on applications given under Important Instructions below.

content_sections.heading: Posts, Eligibility and Pay
content_sections.text: All posts carry the same honorarium of Rs.45,000/- (Rupees Forty five thousand only) per month and Rs.5,000/- (Rupees five thousand only) per month towards conveyance charges. The same qualification applies to all 11 posts. A person shall be qualified for appointment as Special Judicial Magistrate of II-Class if the person: held any post in Andhra Pradesh State Judicial Service and retired or resigned; or held a post in the Andhra Pradesh Judicial Ministerial Service not below the rank of Superintendent (Category-III) of the Andhra Pradesh Judicial Ministerial Subordinate Service Rules, 2019 in the State of Andhra Pradesh and has a Law Degree; or held a post of Section Officer and above in the Andhra Pradesh High Court Service and has a Law Degree; or practised as an Advocate at least for five years and at present is not on the rolls of the Bar Council; or is a retired Gazetted Officer possessing a Law Degree or who has passed the Criminal Judicial Test in full (Indian Penal Code and the Code of Criminal Procedure, or the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 and Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023) conducted by the A.P. Public Service Commission, and who has exercised Magisterial powers during his tenure of service for not less than three years. A suitable retired Judicial Officer shall be given preference. An applicant under clause (iv) (advocate) shall enclose a certificate from the competent authority that he had a practice at the Bar for not less than five years, together with a Certificate of Suspension of Practice issued by the State Bar Association. An applicant who is a Retired Officer of the Revenue Department shall enclose a certificate from the competent authority that he exercised Magisterial powers for not less than three years during his tenure of service in the Gazetted cadre. Non-practising advocates with a practice at the Bar of not less than five years must be above 45 years and below 65 years of age. Retired persons must have at least one and half years (1½ years) to complete 65 years of age. Age is counted as on the date of Notification (21 November 2026). content_sections.heading: Enclosures
content_sections.text: Enclose the following, as per applicability: Attested photocopy of SSC or SSLC Certificate (for age proof). Attested copies of Educational Qualifications including Law and Bar Enrollment Certificate. For Advocates: a certificate of previous practice for not less than 5 years from the concerned Bar Association. Non-practising certificate issued by the State Bar Council. For retired candidates: attested copies of proof of Departmental Tests passed (four papers in IPC & CRPC). Certificate of proof of exercising Magisterial powers for not less than three years during tenure, if the applicant worked as a Gazetted Officer in the Revenue Department. For retired employees: attested copy of Retirement Proceedings.

faq.question: Q1. For how many courts are Special Judicial Magistrate of II-Class applications invited?
faq.answer: Applications are invited for Special Judicial Magistrate of II-Class posts at 11 courts: Chirala, Giddalur, Kandukur, Markapur, three courts at Ongole, Addanki, Darsi, Kanigiri and Podili.

faq.question: Q2. What is the last date to apply for Prakasam District Court Recruitment 2026?
faq.answer: Applications must be received on or before 19 December 2026 up to 5:00 PM. Postal or courier delays will not be considered.

faq.question: Q3. Who is eligible for the Special Judicial Magistrate of II-Class post?
faq.answer: Retired or resigned officers of AP State Judicial Service, Judicial Ministerial staff not below Superintendent or High Court Section Officers and above with a Law Degree, advocates with five years' practice now not on the Bar Council rolls, and retired Gazetted Officers meeting the Law Degree or Criminal Judicial Test and three-year Magisterial power conditions can apply.

faq.question: Q4. What is the age limit?
faq.answer: Non-practising advocates must be above 45 years and below 65 years, and retired persons must have at least 1½ years to complete 65 years, as on the date of Notification.

faq.question: Q5. What is the honorarium for a Special Judicial Magistrate of II-Class?
faq.answer: The honorarium is Rs.45,000 per month plus Rs.5,000 per month towards conveyance charges, subject to enhancement by the Government from time to time.

faq.question: Q6. Can a practising advocate apply?
faq.answer: No. A practising advocate is disqualified; an advocate must have practised for at least five years and at present not be on the rolls of the Bar Council.

faq.question: Q7. What are the court working hours?
faq.answer: The Special Judicial Magistrate of II-Class holds court five days a week, Monday to Friday, on working days from 7.30 am to 10.30 am.

faq.question: Q8. How long will the courts at Addanki, Darsi, Kanigiri and Podili function?
faq.answer: These courts (Sl.No.8 to 11) are sanctioned under the 13th Finance Commission, and their term will be till 31 March 2027.

faq.question: Q9. How much leave does a Special Judicial Magistrate of II-Class get?
faq.answer: The magistrate is entitled to Casual Leave not exceeding 15 days in a calendar year and is not entitled to any other kind of leave.

faq.question: Q10. Who is given preference in selection?
faq.answer: A suitable retired Judicial Officer shall be given preference, and the method of appointment is as mentioned in Notification No.19/SO/2024.
